BPCL: Jefferies retains Buy with a reduced target of ₹380 from ₹410 after a Q2 earnings beat driven by refining, while warning that crude prices around $120 per barrel are putting severe pressure on marketing margins; Citi also retains Buy with a ₹360 target.

ADANI ENERGY SOLUTIONS: Jefferies retains Buy with a reduced target of ₹1,980 from ₹2,060, raising FY27 EBITDA estimates by 6% but cutting FY28–30 estimates by 4–5% due to lower transmission and smart-meter capitalisation guidance.

BSE: Motilal Oswal upgrades the stock to Buy, citing improving derivatives activity, expected FY27 F&O turnover of ₹216 lakh Cr and projected FY26–28 revenue and PAT CAGRs of 23% and 27%, respectively.

DIXON TECHNOLOGIES: Chinese smartphone brands' combined Indian market share falls to 68% in the September quarter amid AI-driven chip shortages and higher prices, while Samsung regains the top position in shipments.

REAL ESTATE / AUTO STOCKS: SBI Chairman reportedly expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 50 basis points in December; any hike could affect borrowing costs and demand, but the move remains a forecast rather than a confirmed policy decision.

BIOCON: Signs an agreement with Janssen Sciences Ireland to commercialise its proposed Yesintek biosimilar to Stelara in nine additional markets, including Australia, Brazil, China and South Korea, subject to regulatory approvals.

ESAF SMALL FINANCE BANK: Completes migration to Oracle FLEXCUBE on October 26, 2026, upgrading core banking, data-centre infrastructure and allied systems; all banking services have been restored following the transition.

GAYATRI PROJECTS: Repays all outstanding fund-based bank and financial-institution borrowings, becoming debt-free in respect of these facilities and reducing its debt-servicing burden.

BGR ENERGY SYSTEMS: Promoter S. K. Sridhar seeks reclassification to the public category for 104 shares, representing 0.0001% of total equity, subject to the SEBI regulatory process.

CORDelia CRUISES: Begins simultaneous two-ship operations from Mumbai and Kochi, expanding itinerary choices across domestic and international routes; Cordelia Sun is scheduled to join the fleet in 2027.

MAHAN INDUSTRIES: Builds digital lending traction through Creditmines, disbursing over ₹25 Cr across 36,000-plus loans within six months and using paperless digital onboarding and credit assessment.

TTK PRESTIGE: Redeems its entire compulsorily convertible debenture investment in GramyaHaat Rural-Tech at an immaterial loss, with no material impact expected on its financial position or operations.

HANNAH JOSEPH HOSPITAL: Receives the CII TN Medclave 2026 Healthcare Excellence Award in Neurosciences in the Above 100 Beds category, recognising its multidisciplinary neuroscience services.

3CIT: Receives a domestic order from Global Education for supplying 1,410 HP desktops across multiple locations, including Pune, Nagpur and Jalgaon.

DECCAN GOLD: Receives Spanish government support of up to €250,000 in deductions for La Brujas exploration costs, with the exploration programme expected to begin in November–December.

📍 BROKERAGE VIEW

IDFC FIRST BANK: UBS retains Neutral with an ₹82 target, while Goldman Sachs maintains Neutral at ₹85; both highlight healthy core revenue growth and loan momentum, balanced by NIM pressure and elevated operating costs.

KOTAK MAHINDRA BANK: Bernstein maintains Market Perform with a ₹500 target, while CLSA retains Outperform at ₹485, citing strong loan growth and fee-income improvement but continued NIM pressure from FCNR-related inflows.

INDUSIND BANK: HSBC maintains Buy with a ₹1,180 target, Jefferies retains Buy with a reduced ₹1,130 target, CLSA maintains Hold at ₹910, UBS retains Sell at ₹870, Macquarie maintains Underperform at ₹760, and Bernstein maintains Outperform at ₹1,000, reflecting improving asset quality and fees but differing views on margin recovery and sustainable returns.

AU SMALL FINANCE BANK: JPMorgan maintains Overweight with a ₹1,165 target, while Kotak Institutional Equities retains Reduce at ₹950, citing strong earnings and loan growth but differing views on credit costs and margin pressures.

📍 ORDER WIN

JYOTISTRUC: Wins two Power Grid Corporation orders worth a combined ₹949.35 Cr, excluding GST, for ±800 kV HVDC transmission lines in Rajasthan, with execution scheduled over 38 months.

SRM CONTRACTORS: Secures a ₹138.37 Cr MoRTH contract for treatment and stabilisation of four landslide-prone locations on the Pithoragarh–Tawaghat road in Uttarakhand, to be completed within 18 months.

RITCO LOGISTICS: Secures transportation contracts worth ₹119.55 Cr in September, including ₹73.67 Cr from BPCL and ₹35.34 Cr from HPCL Rajasthan Refinery, alongside growing TrucksUp platform activity.

SIYARAM RECYCLING: Wins a ₹17.28 Cr export order from Dubai-based Green Metals FZCO for brass billets, to be executed within 30 days.

CSML: Wins two indoor amusement and family entertainment centre projects worth approximately ₹14 Cr, including a ₹9 Cr project in Nagpur and a ₹5 Cr contract with a South Indian operator.

3CIT: Secures a ₹9.08 Cr order, inclusive of GST, from Global Education for supplying 1,410 HP desktops across locations including Pune, Nagpur and Jalgaon.

SUGSLLOYD: Wins a ₹3.16 Cr contract from Tata Power-DDL to supply, install, test and commission 11 kV auto-reclosers and distribution automation systems, valid through October 2027.

ORIENTAL RAIL INFRA: Secures a ₹1.37 Cr Indian Railways order to manufacture, supply and install nine sets of seats and berths for Bangladesh Railway coaches, with execution due by June 30, 2027.

📍 ACQUISITION

WEALTH: Agrees to acquire a 51% stake in Wealth First Advisors for approximately ₹52.10 Cr through cash and share-swap consideration; the board also approved a preferential issue worth up to ₹12.10 Cr.

📍 COLLABORATION

L&T TECHNOLOGY SERVICES: Signs a five-year engineering and R&D contract with Nokia, establishing a dedicated Indian development centre to support AI infrastructure, next-generation computing, 5G networks and software engineering; contract value undisclosed.

BRIGADE: Signs management agreements with Hyatt Hotels Corporation for two Hyatt Regency hotels in Bengaluru, adding approximately 600 rooms across Brigade Global Park and Whitefield–Kadugodi Road.

HCLTECH: Opens two development centres in Bengaluru and Hubli with Rapidus Corporation to support advanced semiconductor engineering, including mask design, process design kits and chip-layout development.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

No relevant leadership changes reported.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

MBEL: Commences Phase-I commercial production at its Sanand PEB facility, increasing capacity by 20,000 MTPA to 92,000 MTPA and total PEB capacity across its plants to 1,23,800 MTPA.

ASTER DM: Kerala government appoints a committee to examine excessive private-hospital treatment costs and is preparing legislation to address charges for surgeries, room rent and diagnostics.

BEL / MAZAGON DOCK / GARDEN REACH SHIPBUILDERS / COCHIN SHIPYARD: Defence Acquisition Council agenda includes a proposed ₹75,000 Cr programme for 13,000-tonne warships for Indian shipyards; the project remains at the conceptual stage, with detailed design expected to take four to five years.

BRIGADE: Expands its hospitality development pipeline through two planned Hyatt Regency properties in Bengaluru, targeting business travel, conferences, social events and leisure demand.

STERLITE TECHNOLOGIES: Remains on track to achieve its FY29 revenue guidance of ₹20,000 Cr, citing disproportionate growth from North America, and raises its FY29 margin guidance to 30% from 27%.

DECCAN GOLD: Reports tungsten and tungsten-tin mineralisation in all eight holes drilled at Spain's Logrosan project; preliminary modelling suggests a deposit exceeding 2.3 million tonnes, with further exploration and assays pending.

SUDEEP PHARMA: Receives Gujarat FDA approval to commence manufacturing at its Nandesari greenfield facility, adding 51,200 MT of annual capacity, with commercial supplies expected in H2 FY27 following customer qualification.

DYNAMIC CABLES: Commences production at its new Reengus manufacturing facility in Rajasthan, expected to increase installed production capacity by approximately 20%.

ATHER ENERGY: Approves up to ₹122 Cr in capacity expansion at Hosur and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, targeting combined annual production capacity of 11.45 lakh units, with phased commissioning through FY28.

📍 FUNDRAISING

ATHER ENERGY: Allots approximately 1.08 Cr equity shares at ₹1,202 per share through a QIP, raising about ₹1,300 Cr; separately, 79.36 lakh warrants at ₹1,260 each aggregating ₹1,000 Cr were approved, alongside manufacturing expansion plans.

FRATELLI VINEYARDS: Approves a rights issue of up to 33.19 lakh partly paid-up shares at ₹90 each, raising approximately ₹29.87 Cr; the record date is October 30, with the issue scheduled from November 6 to November 17, 2026.

VRL LOGISTICS: Announces a buyback of up to 87.5 lakh shares, representing 5% of paid-up equity, at ₹320 per share for an aggregate amount of up to ₹280 Cr.

MAHAN INDUSTRIES: Reports over ₹25 Cr in digital loan disbursements across more than 36,000 loans through its Creditmines platform in under six months since commencing lending in May 2026.

ITC HOTELS: Approves incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai with a proposed equity investment of up to ₹20 Cr to operate hotels, restaurants and related hospitality businesses, subject to approvals.

BIGBLOC: Material subsidiary Bigbloc Building Elements approves an IPO in principle, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals; issue size, pricing and timing remain undecided, and it will remain a subsidiary after the proposed listing.

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

MUTHOOT MICROFIN: CareEdge Global raises the outlook on its BB- foreign-currency rating to Positive from Stable for $50 million in existing and proposed external commercial borrowings, supported by improving collections, AUM growth and lower credit costs.

📍 FII STAKE CHANGES / BOUGHT-SOLD

No relevant FII stake changes reported.

📍 IPO

BIGBLOC: Material subsidiary Bigbloc Building Elements approves plans for an IPO, subject to shareholder, SEBI and stock-exchange approvals; the parent company will retain subsidiary status after the proposed listing.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

IDFC FIRST BANK: Reports Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹1,045 Cr, up 196.5% YoY, with NII rising 21% YoY and core operating profit growing 38.5%; NIM moderates to 5.58%, while management targets recovery to approximately 5.8% by Q4 FY27.

KOTAK MAHINDRA BANK: Reports 29% YoY EPS growth, supported by 25% YoY balance-sheet growth; corporate and SME lending drive loan expansion, while FCNR-related inflows contribute to NIM compression.

INDUSIND BANK: Reports Q2 PAT of approximately ₹1,240 Cr, with standalone profit up 17% QoQ, improved asset quality and stronger fee income; NIM declines to 3.23%, while management retains its 1% exit RoA ambition for FY27.

AU SMALL FINANCE BANK: Reports Q2 FY27 NII growth of 32% YoY, PPoP growth of 25% and PAT growth of 53%; gross advances rise 27.9% YoY, CASA improves to 29.5%, and credit costs moderate to 0.70% of assets.

SUPREME INDUSTRIES: Targets approximately 10% volume growth for FY27, with plastic piping volumes rising 24% in Q2; capacity expansion continues across multiple locations, while polymer-price volatility and geopolitical risks remain key considerations.

SAKAR HEALTHCARE: Reports Q2 gross profit growth of 53% YoY to ₹41.68 Cr and H1 growth of 57% to ₹80.07 Cr; oncology commercial supplies have commenced, with 22 marketing authorisations granted and further international approvals supporting expansion.

DRC SYSTEMS: Reports EBITDA margins of 29% for Q2 and 31% for H1, supported by its AI-first delivery model and operational efficiency, with continued traction across eLearning, AI agents and enterprise solutions.

JSW STEEL: Expects coking coal costs to rise by $25 per tonne in Q3 FY27 versus $12 per tonne in Q2, while consolidated EBITDA per tonne is expected to improve sequentially.

SHREE CEMENT: Expects better EBITDA per tonne in the upcoming quarter compared with Q2, following 18% volume growth despite seasonally soft conditions.

GNA AXLES: Says Q2 FY27 performance was strong on both revenue and profit, with ₹40 Cr already invested out of ₹780 Cr earmarked for EV and allied segments.

SKYWAYS: Increases India's air-export market share to 6.3% in Q2 FY27 from 6.2% in the previous quarter, advancing to 42nd globally from 44th in chargeable-weight rankings, with expansion planned across Southeast Asia and China.

SAKAR HEALTHCARE: Reports 69 oncology product contracts, 351 global dossiers shared and 22 marketing authorisations granted, alongside ongoing technology transfers and growing international commercial supplies.

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

ZYDUS LIFESCIENCES: USFDA issues five observations following an October inspection of its Moraiya facility, flagging reported data-integrity and quality-control deficiencies; the observations raise regulatory risks, although they do not themselves establish an import alert or production restriction.

ZYDUS LIFESCIENCES: Reports that an Estradiol approval was granted on October 21 for a product to be manufactured at its Moraiya facility after the inspection; the approval provides additional context but does not eliminate the compliance concerns raised by the USFDA observations.

📍 CLARIFICATION

ZYDUS LIFESCIENCES: Analysts indicate that the post-inspection Moraiya approval suggests ongoing regulatory activity at the facility; the approval does not independently confirm that all inspection findings have been resolved.

📍 LAUNCHES

HYUNDAI MOTOR INDIA: Launches the BAYON mid-size SUV at a starting ex-showroom price of ₹9.99 lakh, featuring a 1.5L petrol engine, generative-AI voice assistant and Level 2 Pro ADAS with 23 features; exports are planned to over 50 markets.

MEHUL TELECOM: Opens a new MOBILE.COM franchise retail store in Tankara, Morbi, Gujarat, on October 25, 2026.

GODREJ PROPERTIES: Unveils a 1,400 sq m eco-resort-themed clubhouse at Godrej Hill Retreat in Pune, featuring seven themed gardens and over 25 resort-style amenities, while targeting delivery of more than 4,000 Pune homes by FY27-end.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

SUNITA TOOLS: Signs an agreement to acquire a 50% stake in a Bulgaria-incorporated defence entity through a proposed 50:50 joint venture, targeting access to European and NATO defence markets, subject to due diligence and regulatory approvals.

PANASONIC ENERGY INDIA: Approves the transfer of leasehold rights in its Makarpura industrial plot in Vadodara to an identified buyer, subject to GIDC and other required approvals; transaction value remains undisclosed.

LANDMARK CARS: Receives letters of intent from JSW Motors to establish five dealership outlets across Ahmedabad and Bhopal, adding a new automotive brand to its retail portfolio.

📍 IT NEWS

COFORGE: Named a Leader in Everest Group's Quality Engineering Services for AI Applications and Systems PEAK Matrix Assessment 2026, recognising capabilities in AI validation, generative AI testing, agentic AI assurance and responsible AI.

BHARAT PETROLEUM (BPCL) Q2 CONCALL : TARGETS ₹25,000 CR FY27 CAPEX & ₹40,000–45,000 CR FY28 CAPEX, WITH BINA PETROCHEMICALS & MOZAMBIQUE LNG PROJECTS TARGETING MID-2028 COMPLETION

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS FY27 CAPEX TARGET AT ₹25,000 CR, WITH SPENDING POTENTIALLY EXCEEDING GUIDANCE BY 5–10%

• FY28 CAPEX EXPECTED AT ₹40,000–45,000 CR, EXCLUDING ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR THE PROPOSED ANDHRA REFINERY

• BINA PETROCHEMICAL PROJECT 40.2% COMPLETE, WITH ₹43,367 CR INVESTMENT & COMMISSIONING TARGETED BY MID-2028

• KOCHI POLYPROPYLENE PROJECT 55.1% COMPLETE, WITH ₹4,850 CR INVESTMENT & COMPLETION TARGETED FOR OCTOBER 2027

• MUMBAI PRFCC PROJECT TARGETS SEPTEMBER 2029 COMPLETION, WITH APPROVED INVESTMENT OF ₹13,626 CR

• MOZAMBIQUE LNG PROJECT 47% COMPLETE, WITH FIRST GAS EXPECTED BY MID-2028 & BPCL'S PHASE-1 SHARE ESTIMATED AT 1.3 MMTPA

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS CUSTOMER TIE-UPS FOR APPROXIMATELY 1 MMTPA MOZAMBIQUE LNG OVER THE NEXT 2–3 QUARTERS

• PROPOSED ANDHRA REFINERY PLANNED AT 10 MMTPA CAPACITY WITH 32–33% PETROCHEMICAL INTENSITY; FINAL INVESTMENT DECISION PENDING

• MUMBAI SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL PROJECT PHASE-1 COMMISSIONING TARGETED FOR JANUARY 2027

• REFINERY CAPACITY UTILIZATION REACHED 117%, WITH Q2 THROUGHPUT AT 10.4 MMT & REPORTED GRM AT $32.53/BARREL

• GRM ADJUSTED FOR SAED STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY $14/BARREL; MANAGEMENT EXPECTS STRONG REFINING SPREADS TO CONTINUE, SUBJECT TO MARKET CONDITIONS

• REFINERY UTILIZATION MAY DECLINE DURING Q3–Q4 FY27 DUE TO PLANNED MAINTENANCE AT MUMBAI, KOCHI & BINA

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS PETROL DEMAND GROWTH OF 5–6%, WHILE DIESEL DEMAND GROWTH COULD REACH 3.5–4%

• LPG UNDERRECOVERIES EXPECTED TO INCREASE TO ₹328 PER CYLINDER IN NOVEMBER VS APPROXIMATELY ₹290 Q2 AVERAGE; ADDITIONAL GOVERNMENT COMPENSATION REMAINS UNCERTAIN

• STANDALONE DEBT/EQUITY AT 0.16X, BUT HIGHER CAPEX MAY INCREASE LEVERAGE; ELEVATED CRUDE PRICES, NARROWING RUSSIAN CRUDE DISCOUNTS & PROJECT EXECUTION REMAIN KEY RISKS

ITC HOTELS: APPROVES WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY IN DUBAI; PLANS INVESTMENT OF UP TO ₹20 CR

• Global Expansion: Board approved incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE)

• Investment: Proposed investment of up to ₹20 Cr through equity subscription in multiple tranches

• Ownership: ITC Hotels will hold 100% equity in the proposed subsidiary

• Business Operations: New entity will operate hotels, restaurants and other hospitality-related businesses

• International Presence: Dubai subsidiary could support expansion into overseas hospitality markets

• Regulatory Approvals: Incorporation subject to necessary approvals from Dubai authorities

• Project Status: Subsidiary is yet to be incorporated; operational and expansion details have not been announced

Impact: Positive (Proposed Dubai subsidiary strengthens ITC Hotels' international expansion strategy and creates potential long-term growth opportunities, subject to execution and regulatory approvals.)

ANANTAM HIGHWAYS TRUST Q2 CONCALL : TARGETS ₹2.75 QUARTERLY DISTRIBUTION PER UNIT, PLANS 18 ROAD ASSET ACQUISITIONS OVER 18–24 MONTHS & AIMS TO IMPROVE TRADING LIQUIDITY

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS TO MAINTAIN ₹2.75 QUARTERLY DISTRIBUTION PER UNIT AS A BASE, WITH GRADUAL INCREASES TARGETED OVER TIME

• QUARTERLY DISTRIBUTION UP 10% TO ₹2.75 PER UNIT VS ₹2.50 PREVIOUSLY, IMPLYING AN ANNUALIZED RUN RATE OF ₹11 PER UNIT

• MANAGEMENT IDENTIFIED 18 ROAD ASSETS IN ITS RIGHT OF FIRST OFFER (ROFO) PIPELINE, WITH POTENTIAL ACQUISITIONS OVER THE NEXT 18–24 MONTHS

• ROFO PIPELINE INCLUDES 11 ASSETS LINKED TO DILIP BUILDCON & 7 ASSETS ASSOCIATED WITH ALPHA ALTERNATIVES

• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO GRADUALLY ACQUIRE ROFO ASSETS, SUBJECT TO VALUATIONS, FUNDING AVAILABILITY & REGULATORY APPROVALS

• PREVIOUSLY PROPOSED ROFO ACQUISITION & ASSOCIATED PREFERENTIAL ALLOTMENT DEFERRED DUE TO TIMING, PRICING & REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS

• MANAGEMENT INTENDS TO REVISIT THE DEFERRED ACQUISITION, BUT NO REVISED COMPLETION TIMELINE HAS BEEN ANNOUNCED

• FUTURE ACQUISITIONS WILL FOCUS ON NAV-ACCRETIVE & IRR-ACCRETIVE TRANSACTIONS, RATHER THAN PORTFOLIO EXPANSION ALONE

• ACQUISITIONS MAY BE FUNDED THROUGH FRESH EQUITY, INVIT UNIT SWAPS & ADDITIONAL DEBT, WITH THIRD-PARTY ROAD ASSETS ALSO UNDER CONSIDERATION

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS IMPROVEMENT IN TRADING LIQUIDITY & EXPANSION OF THE INVESTOR BASE OVER THE NEXT 6–12 MONTHS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS HIGHER INTEREST RATES TO SUPPORT HAM ANNUITY CASH FLOWS, WITH BORROWING STRATEGY FOCUSED ON T-BILL & MCLR-LINKED DEBT

• Q2 REVENUE AT ₹158.2 CR, EBITDA AT ₹131.9 CR & EBITDA MARGIN AT 83.38%, WHILE PROFIT BEFORE TAX UP 8.88% QOQ TO ₹96.9 CR

• OUTSTANDING DEBT DOWN ₹91 CR QOQ TO ₹1,852 CR, WITH AAA/STABLE CREDIT RATINGS MAINTAINED

ZYDUS LIFESCIENCES: USFDA FLAGS SERIOUS DATA INTEGRITY ISSUES AT MORAIYA PLANT; ISSUES 5 OBSERVATIONS

• USFDA Inspection: Issued 5 observations following inspection of the Moraiya manufacturing facility in Gujarat during October 5–13, 2026

• US Revenue Exposure: Approximately 45% of Zydus's US sales reportedly originate from products manufactured at Moraiya

• Data Integrity Issues: Microbial growth detected during testing was allegedly not accurately recorded in laboratory records

• Product Quality: FDA flagged inadequate investigation of metal contamination in a tablet that resulted in a Class II recall

• Quality Control Failures: Multiple batches exceeding established assay control limits reportedly entered the US market without adequate root-cause investigations

• Compliance Gaps: Inadequate written procedures for identifying, investigating and reporting suspect or illegitimate drug products

• Equipment Validation: FTIR instruments used for raw-material identification reportedly lacked documented performance verification for three years

• Raw Material Testing: Reduced testing continued despite previous specification failures, contrary to company procedures

• Regulatory Risk: Observations raise concerns over manufacturing compliance, potential regulatory action and future US product approvals

Impact: Negative (Reported data integrity violations and quality-control deficiencies at a facility with significant US revenue exposure pose regulatory and business risks. The observations do not themselves establish that an import alert or production restriction has been imposed.)

STEEL STRIPS WHEELS – PLANS ₹1,400 CR GREENFIELD CAPEX
Expansion & Capacity Update

Capex Details
- In-principle Board approval received for Maharashtra greenfield facility.
- Total proposed investment stands at ₹1,400 Cr over 60 months.
- Alloy wheels: ₹815 Cr for 2.5 million units annually.
- Steel wheels: ₹410 Cr for 1.8 million units annually.
- Hot stamping: ₹175 Cr for 1.3 million strokes annually.
- Funding through debt and internal accruals.
- Project remains subject to approvals and clearances.

Growth Drivers
- Management expects alloy-wheel market growth of 12% annually.
- Steel-wheel market growth estimated at 4% annually.
- Bhuj expansion adds 1.2 million alloy-wheel capacity.
- Aluminium-knuckle capacity at Bhuj to increase by 0.6 million units.
- H1FY27 steel-wheel capacity utilisation reached 85%.
- Alloy-wheel capacity utilisation stood at 89%.
- FY27 alloy-wheel capacity target stands at approximately 6.2 million units.
- Hot stamping adds passenger-vehicle structural body-part manufacturing capabilities.

Key Monitorables
- Regulatory approvals and project execution timelines.
- Phased capex deployment and funding mix.
- Capacity commissioning and customer ramp-up.
- Incremental ROCE and profitability from new capacities.
- Balance-sheet impact from debt-funded expansion.

Key Takeaway
- Expansion targets higher-margin alloy wheels and product diversification.
- Strong existing utilisation supports the need for additional capacity.
- Returns depend on execution, demand and capacity utilisation.
- Debt levels and incremental ROCE remain critical monitorables.
- No Recommendations.

SPECIALISED CHEMICAL – CAPACITY CONSTRAINTS MEET STRONG DEMAND
Business & Investment Analysis

Business Overview
- Specialised chemical used in ceramic catalyst manufacturing.
- Material burns away, leaving precisely structured ceramic pores.
- End applications include diesel exhaust emission-control systems.
- Only two global manufacturers reportedly hold required approvals.
- One manufacturer is reportedly based in Ankleshwar, Gujarat.

Growth Catalysts
- European regulations mandate improved heavy-truck emission-control systems.
- Regulatory changes could drive catalyst demand from 2029.
- Sales increased 32% in the previous financial year.
- Half-year sales growth accelerated to 60%.

Capacity Constraints
- Management estimates revenue capacity at ₹850–900 Cr.
- Current annualised revenue has reached approximately ₹869 Cr.
- Existing manufacturing facilities are approaching capacity limits.
- New plant commissioning is expected around April 2028.

Key Risks
- One customer contributes 35% of total revenue.
- Operating cash conversion remains weak.
- Only around one-third of operating profit converted into cash.
- Capacity constraints could limit near-term growth.
- Expansion delays could restrict demand fulfilment.

Key Takeaway
- Regulatory demand creates a potential long-term growth opportunity.
- Capacity expansion timing is critical for growth realisation.
- Customer concentration and cash conversion require close monitoring.
- Exact chemical identity and company require further verification.
- Impact: Potentially Positive, Execution-Dependent

CHEMCON SPECIALITY CHEMICALS Q2 FY27

• Net Profit ₹7.52 Cr ↑30.84% YoY, ↓31.41% QoQ

• Revenue ₹65.45 Cr ↑21.85% YoY, ↓1.56% QoQ

• EBITDA ₹11.04 Cr ↑61.00% YoY, ↓28.47% QoQ

• Margin 16.87% vs 12.76% YoY, 23.21% QoQ

CHEMBOND CHEMICALS Q2 CONCALL

• Strong revenue growth momentum expected to continue in H2 FY27.

• Q4 FY27 expected to benefit from historically strong seasonal demand.

• ₹1,000 Cr revenue ambition reiterated, supported by organic expansion and potential acquisitions.

• Raw material cost pressure expected to continue in Q3 at levels similar to Q2.

• EBITDA margin at 8.8% vs approximately 16.2% QoQ, impacted by higher material costs.

• Margin recovery expected within 1–2 quarters after raw material costs and supply chains normalize.

• Water Technologies revenue up 28% YoY in H1, supported by strong industrial demand.

• Water treatment chemical volumes up approximately 44% YoY.

• Data center water treatment business expanding, with customers including NTT, Yotta and CtrlS.

• New-age industries' contribution to Water Technologies revenue targeted to rise to 12–15% over three years from 7–8% currently.

• Construction Chemicals revenue up 30% YoY in H1, with increasing focus on sealants.

• Chemical Distribution revenue up 86% YoY, while Cleaning & Hygiene business grew 59% in H1.

• Equipment order book stands at approximately ₹15–20 Cr for FY27, with recurring chemical consumables supporting revenue visibility.

• Management evaluating synergistic acquisitions, with no major manufacturing capacity constraints for future expansion.

• Key risks include raw material inflation, fixed-price public sector contracts, delayed margin recovery and acquisition execution.

KOTAK MAHINDRA BANK Q2 FY27 CONCALL

• Long-term loan growth targeted at 1.5–2× nominal GDP growth.

• Core advances up 19% YoY, excluding FCNR-backed loans and KMIL portfolio transfer.

• Mobilised ₹55,344 Cr through FCNR-B deposits, with remaining liquidity to be deployed over coming quarters.

• NIM at 4.31% vs 4.53% QoQ, impacted by approximately 15 bps from FCNR-B-related transactions.

• NIM recovery expected from loan repricing and liquidity deployment, with greater benefits anticipated in Q4.

• Approximately 65–70% of the loan portfolio is floating-rate, supporting repricing benefits.

• Credit cost declined to 35 bps from 46 bps QoQ, reflecting disciplined underwriting.

• Gross NPA at 1.04% vs 1.18% QoQ, while Net NPA declined to 0.24%.

• CASA ratio excluding FCNR-B improved to 41.8% from 40.3% QoQ.

• SME advances up 27% YoY to approximately ₹1.4 lakh Cr, remaining a key growth priority.

• Corporate banking advances up 25% YoY, while fee income grew 36%.

• Gradual expansion of unsecured retail lending planned, with focus on existing customers and credit quality.

• Technology spending expected at around 13% of operating expenses, focused on AI, automation and cost efficiency.

• ECL transition expected to have a one-time impact below 2% of net worth; earlier estimates indicated 12–15 bps additional recurring credit cost, subject to regulatory clarity.

• Key risks include FCNR-B liquidity deployment, NIM pressure, rural credit risks, ECL transition and capital market volatility.

PERMANENT MAGNETS Q2 CONCALL

• FY27 revenue growth guidance at 20–30%, supported by EV demand and export orders.

• FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20–25% vs approximately 25% in Q2.

• Automotive revenue ₹24 Cr ↑129% YoY, driven by strong export EV demand.

• EV demand expected to remain near Q2 levels through H2 FY27.

• Alloys revenue targeted at ₹40–50 Cr in FY27, with improved capacity utilisation expected in H2.

• Alloys revenue could reach ₹70–80 Cr in FY28, subject to successful capacity ramp-up.

• Alloys business expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven or marginally positive margins in FY27.

• Relay pilot supplies expected in H2 FY27, with commercialisation targeted for FY28.

• Relay business offers potential gross margins of 15–30%, subject to customer approvals and execution.

• Quantum Magnetics Phase 2 commissioned in October 2026, with commercial ramp-up expected in FY28, subject to approvals.

• Quantum Magnetics FY28 revenue potential indicated at ₹10–40 Cr, without firm management guidance.

• Quantum Phase 2 installed capacity has indicative annual revenue potential of ₹40–60 Cr, depending on product mix.

• ECMS approval received for incentives equivalent to 25% of eligible capex, subject to scheme conditions.

• Plant consolidation could generate annual savings of ₹5 Cr over time.

• Key risks include EV demand sustainability, alloys utilisation, relay approval delays, quantum commercialisation and dependence on Chinese imports.

Swiggy – HSBC

• Rating: Hold

• Target Price: Cut to ₹240 from ₹315

• Q2FY27 showed some improvement in operating metrics, but not enough to boost confidence in long-term guidance.

• Instamart growth improved, but its relatively smaller scale remains a challenge in achieving EBITDA break-even.

• Market share losses in Food Delivery and rising competition remain key concerns.

Swiggy – CLSA

• Rating: Outperform

• Target Price: Cut to ₹262

• Q2FY27 Instamart NOV growth accelerated QoQ to 13.4%, but remained below expectations, with wider-than-expected losses.

• Food Delivery adjusted EBITDA was in line with CLSA estimates but missed consensus expectations.

• The performance gap with Eternal widened in both businesses, particularly in profitability.

• Swiggy remains confident of a turnaround in Instamart's growth and profitability.

• CLSA believes rebuilding investor confidence will require consistent improvement over the next few quarters.

• Despite low investor expectations, CLSA sees significant opportunities across categories.

Swiggy – Nomura

• Rating: Buy

• Target Price: Cut to ₹300

• Food Delivery business continues to perform steadily and remains a key cash generator.

• Nomura expects the Food Delivery business to generate ₹1,300–1,900 crore EBITDA in FY27–FY28.

• Quick Commerce execution continues to fall short of expectations.

• Food Delivery valued at 40x FY28E EBITDA, unchanged and in line with Eternal.

• Nomura assigns no value to the Quick Commerce business or its cash balances due to limited conviction.

• Despite QC-related concerns, Nomura believes the disappointment is largely priced in, making the risk-reward favourable.

Ola Electric – Goldman Sachs

• Rating: Downgraded to Sell

• Target Price: Cut to ₹23

• Goldman Sachs sees a more challenging path to free cash flow due to high interest costs, capex requirements and prolonged operating losses.

• Revenue needs to grow 3.6x–7.1x over FY26 levels by FY28–FY30 to cover current capex and interest obligations.

• Battery cell business faces potential operational challenges following the departure of its business head.

• FY27–FY29 revenue estimates cut by up to 10%, factoring in tougher market-share conditions versus two-wheeler peers.

• Key factors that could improve the outlook:
• Recovery in the electric two-wheeler business through a dealer-led sales and service model.

• Positive consolidated operating EBITDA margin.

• More customer wins and improved profitability in the battery cell business.

KEI Industries – HSBC

• Rating: Hold

• Target Price: Cut to ₹4,450

• Strong Q2FY27 revenue growth was overshadowed by weak margins, resulting in an earnings miss.

• Earnings growth is expected to remain strong, with a projected 20% EPS CAGR over FY26–FY29.

• Rising competition remains a key risk.

• Target price cut due to lower earnings forecasts.

KEI Industries – CLSA

• Rating: Upgraded to Outperform

• Target Price: Cut to ₹4,845

• CLSA believes competition risks and the marginal guidance cut are largely factored in after the recent stock correction.

• Q2FY27 PAT came in slightly below estimates despite strong revenue growth due to lower margins.

• FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 25%, with volume growth guidance of 10%+.

• EBITDA margin guidance is expected to be at the lower end of the earlier 11–12% range.

• Capacity expansion supports medium-term growth of 20%+.

• Competitive and supply-side risks appear largely priced in, according to CLSA.

CreditAccess Grameen – HSBC

• Rating: Buy

• Target Price: Cut to ₹1,400

• Profitability, currently well above through-the-cycle levels, is expected to normalise going forward.

• HSBC cut EPS estimates by 3.6–4.9% for FY27–FY28, factoring in lower AUM growth in FY27, fee compression and higher provisions.

• Target price cut as the cyclical downturn deepens.

• Despite near-term challenges, HSBC believes the current market price offers value.

CreditAccess Grameen – CLSA

• Rating: Outperform

• Target Price: Cut to ₹1,600

• Q2FY27 PPOP beat estimates by 7%, driven by better NII.

• PAT remained in line with estimates due to the creation of a macroprudential buffer.

• Management raised FY27 ROA guidance by around 100 bps after ROA exceeded guidance for the second consecutive quarter.

• AUM growth accelerated to 19%, led by retail finance, which accounts for around 25% of AUM and continues to report lower delinquencies.

• Net slippages rose around 70 bps QoQ but remain below steady-state levels.

• Management expects some increase in credit costs in Q3FY27 due to drought conditions.

• CLSA cut FY28–FY29 PAT estimates by 2–4%, factoring in another repo rate hike and the impact of draft insurance distribution guidelines.

Havells India – HSBC

• Rating: Buy

• Target Price: ₹1,400

• Strong results with revenue beating consensus estimates, while profit remained largely in line.

• Margin pressure was mainly driven by the Cables & Wires (C&W) segment.

• Management indicated that further price hikes of around 5–7% across products may be required in Q3FY27.

Havells India – Jefferies

• Rating: Hold

• Target Price: ₹1,220

• September quarter sales surged 35% YoY, driven by Cables & Wires (copper price pass-through) and double-digit volume growth in switchgears.

• Low base in the room air conditioner (RAC) segment also supported growth.

• PAT grew 11% YoY, in line with Jefferies' estimates, as other income declined sharply due to a one-off gain in the previous year.

• Operating margin remained firm at 9%, supported by price hikes of around 10–15% over the past 12 months.

• Management is evaluating a further 5–7% price hike in Q3FY27.

• Capex outlook remains unchanged, with a focus on R&D and the Cables & Wires segment.

• Jefferies estimates 15% PAT CAGR over FY27–FY29.

Havells India – Nomura

• Rating: Neutral

• Target Price: ₹1,232

• Q2FY27 EBITDA came in above estimates.

• Price hikes are driving growth, but rising competition remains a key risk to margin recovery.

• Increasing competitive pressure could create margin headwinds.

• Stock trades at 32x FY28E EPS, which Nomura considers the fair-value zone.

Colgate-Palmolive India – Jefferies

• Rating: Buy

• Target Price: Cut to ₹2,000

• Reported double-digit topline growth, partly supported by the GST transition base effect.

• Two-year revenue CAGR stood at just 3%.

• Advertising spends increased to around 19% of revenue, reaching a multi-quarter high.

• Higher brand investments supported growth initiatives but weighed on EBITDA margins.

• New CEO expects strong growth ahead, driven by a science-backed product portfolio and continued investments.

• Jefferies cut EPS estimates by 3–4%.

**KOTAK UPDATES - RATING CHANGES**

**CUMMINS INDIA - UPGRADE TO BUY**
- Fair Value: ₹5,300 vs ₹5,600 earlier
- Expected upside: 20%
- Data centres expected to support 8% of revenue growth
- Non-DC business revenue CAGR estimated at 9% for FY26-30
- Distribution ownership and supply-chain strengths support competitiveness
- Parent relationships with hyperscalers could improve customer stickiness
- Domestic and Chinese competition may cap margin expansion
- Most available cost-efficiency benefits are already captured
- Margins expected to decline during FY26-30
- Stock trades at 39x FY28E EPS
- PAT CAGR estimated at 16% over FY26-30

**ETERNAL - BUY**
- Fair Value: ₹435 vs ₹395 earlier
- Blinkit NOV growth reached 22% QoQ and 79% YoY
- Blinkit delivered 30 bps sequential EBITDA margin improvement
- Food delivery NOV grew 21% YoY
- Food delivery EBITDA margin stood at 5.5% of NOV
- Higher Blinkit store additions drive increased revenue estimates
- Lower food delivery and other margins moderate EBITDA upgrades
- Revised valuation based on the sum-of-the-parts method

**INDIAN HOTELS - ADD**
- Fair Value: ₹820
- EBITDA increased 24% YoY
- RevPAR improved 25% YoY
- Delhi revenue grew 51% amid the BRICS Summit
- Rajasthan revenue grew 25% YoY
- Goa revenue grew 16% YoY
- FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 15-17%
- Earlier revenue guidance stood at 12-14%
- Pipeline stands at 34,800 keys, with 81% managed
- Strong pipeline supports potential double-digit growth

**VMM - BUY**
- Fair Value: ₹125
- Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY
- Revenue came in 3.8% below estimates
- Same-store sales growth stood at 5.4%
- Retail area increased 10.5% YoY
- Revenue miss attributed to festive-season shift into Q3
- FY27-29 EBITDA estimates trimmed by 3-4%
- Lower projected revenue growth drives estimate reductions

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Cummins India upgraded to BUY despite lower fair value
- Data centres remain a key growth driver for Cummins
- Eternal's Blinkit growth exceeded expectations
- Indian Hotels raised FY27 revenue growth guidance
- VMM's revenue miss reflects festive-season timing
- Kotak retains positive ratings across all four stocks

KOTAK Sec Raises Eternal Target to Rs 435 per share

Blinkit delivered an impressive 2QFY27 performance, with NOV growth of 22%/79% qoq/yoy, surpassing our expectations. It posted 30 bps sequential EBITDA margin improvement. 

Zomato’s food delivery NOV growth came in at 21% yoy, ahead of estimates, although EBITDA margin at 5.5% of NOV came in slightly below expectations. 

We increase our revenue estimates for Blinkit, as we bake in higher store addition. Overall EBITDA increase is moderated by lower margin assumptions for food delivery and others. 

Changes in estimates drive a revised SoTP-based FV of Rs435 (Rs395 earlier).

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.
